notes: Recorded from the shipped artifact: course/assets/print.css (world layer, injected by nav.js on every page before nav.css and any page stylesheet), tools/hub-template.html (hub component layer, source of the generated index.html), course/assets/lesson.css (reading sheet, including its engraving layer and the fixes from the finish review), course/assets/nav.css (persistent side index).

The palette and lettering are Anthropic's own, read off anthropic.com. Anthropic's licensed faces (Styrene A / anthropicSans, Copernicus / anthropicSerif) are NOT in this repo: Hanken Grotesk stands in for the sans, Faustina for the serif. JetBrains Mono is the real face Anthropic ships. All self-hosted from npm Fontsource under course/assets/fonts/ with OFL-LICENSE-fontsource.txt alongside.
This record supersedes the earlier green-and-oxblood / Bodoni Moda + Archivo + Chivo Mono record. Those three font files were deleted from the repo.

The type ramp in the frontmatter is the ramp the build actually ships (rem against a 17px root on the reading sheet, px against a 15px body on the workbench, plus SVG diagram lettering). It is deliberately not an idealised scale.

narrative.overview:
This is a certificate press running on Anthropic's own colour and lettering. The craft is security printing - hairline rules, ruled ledgers, plate serials, engraved figures, a counterfoil, a guilloche rosette - because a weighted score report and a credential are both documents that earn trust by being unreproducibly precise. The stock and the inks, however, are read straight off anthropic.com: the warm slate-to-ivory ramp, clay as the single accent, olive and their error red as the two semantic inks, their focus blue on the focus ring. Dark is the steel plate and remains the default; light is ivory.

Density is high and deliberately unpadded. Nothing is a card floating in space; everything sits in a ruled structure that says where it belongs. Two surfaces share the world through course/assets/print.css, which nav.js injects on every page ahead of nav.css and any page stylesheet: the hub is a workbench set in the grotesque at a 15px px ramp, and the course is a reading sheet set in Faustina at a 17px root with a rem ramp. The originally specified didone display face is gone - display is now the grotesque at 700 with easier tracking - and the world lost nothing, because the engraving was never in the serifs; it is in the line work.

The build refuses the category arrangement it replaced: equal rounded cards on near-black with one blue accent and a progress bar. There are no shadows, no gradients, no radii, and no progress bar - the learning path's track is explicitly hidden and the count is printed instead.
keyCharacteristics: Warm slate/ivory stock with exactly one accent ink, clay; olive reserved to the 720 pass mark.
Square corners everywhere, including rx: 0; ry: 0 on every SVG rect.
Two line weights only: 1px hairline (rule) and 2px plate line (rule-firm).
Flat by construction - depth is line density, never shadow or blur.
Mono serials and tabular figures wherever the page labels or counts.
Ornament lives in structure and never enters a question body or a timed screen.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Clay is the only accent in the system. A new element does not get a new hue; it gets clay, or an ink weight, or a rule.

rules.name: The Deep-Cut Clay Rule
rules.body: True clay #d97757 measures 2.96:1 on ivory. In the light theme, therefore, text and line work take the deeper cut #ad5533 and the true clay is used only as a filled field with slate text on it. Raising light-theme line work back to #d97757 is not a correction; it is a contrast failure.

rules.name: The Reserved Mark Rule
rules.body: Olive means 720. If a new element wants olive, it is claiming to be the pass mark; if it is not one, it takes ink-faint.

rules.name: The Ink-Fill Rule
rules.body: At most one filled colour field per sheet, and it is ink-fill with ink-fill-t on it - the hub's Module 1 block, or a lesson's .path-start. Hovering it empties the field and leaves the outline.

rules.name: The Bare-Plate Rule
rules.body: An empty state is unengraved plate: the low-density line work with nothing cut into it. Never a grey placeholder fill, never a zeroed bar dressed as data.

rules.name: The Unearned Ground Rule
rules.body: A shortfall is drawn in the neutral gap, not in red. Red is reserved for a wrong answer and an expiring clock.

rules.name: The Four Jobs Rule
rules.body: Each face has exactly one job: the grotesque at 700 engraves display, the grotesque at 400-650 runs the workbench, Faustina sets long-form reading, JetBrains Mono sets serials, figures and code. A face outside its job is a bug.

rules.name: The Serial Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels or numbers rather than speaks - plate facts, pills, captions, table heads, breadcrumbs, wayfinding, option keys, figcaptions - is mono, tracked 0.1-0.16em, uppercase, in ink-faint. The eyebrow at the head of a lesson sheet is one of these: a right-aligned plate serial carrying the sheet's own identifier, not a label stacked above the title.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Figures line up everywhere, not only in tables: print.css applies font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to table, .serial, .fig, time and .num globally.

rules.name: The Two Roots Rule
rules.body: The reading sheet is set in rem against a 17px root; the workbench is set in px against a 15px body. Both ramps are real and neither is idealised - do not port one surface's steps onto the other, and do not round the half-pixel steps (13.5px, 14.5px, 11.5px) away: they are the shipped ramp.

rules.name: The Stand-In Rule
rules.body: Do not add an @font-face for Styrene A or Copernicus, and do not reference anthropicSans or anthropicSerif. They are licensed and absent. Any new face must be self-hosted under course/assets/fonts/ with its licence file beside it.

rules.name: The Two Measures Rule
rules.body: Two widths, owned solely by lesson.css: --prose (28rem) is the reading measure and constrains body-level p, ul, ol; --measure (40rem) is the wider structural width for figures, tables, callouts, apparatus and pager. Table, quiz, sidenote, flag, figure, toc, pager, crumb and nav contents are explicitly released from --prose. Separating the two was a deliberate fix - do not collapse them, and do not redefine either outside lesson.css.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Three or more sibling items are ruled rows in one index sharing column tracks - 2px top, 1px between, 1px bottom. If a design reaches for a grid of equal cards, it has left this world.

rules.name: The Printed Count Rule
rules.body: Progress is a printed count, not a bar: .path-progress .track is set to display: none and the number stands alone. Bounded measures that are genuinely quantities - the plan meter, the seven domain bars - are 1px-bordered tracks with a flat clay fill and a 1px olive target line at 72%. That is a ruled gauge, not a progress bar.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that needs to read as raised gets sheet and a hairline. Nothing in this world casts.

rules.name: The Line-Density Rule
rules.body: Where tone is needed, cut more lines. Value is built from stroke count at 0.6px, never from fills or blurs.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0 on every element, and rx/ry are 0 on every SVG rect. Radius is not a variable in this system.

dos: Do take colour from the tokens in print.css only, and let the theme split handle light: tint for line work and text, ink-fill for a filled field.
Do set every radius to 0, and add rx: 0; ry: 0 to any SVG rect you draw.
Do use exactly two rule weights: 1px rule between peers, 2px rule-firm to open or close a structure.
Do set anything that labels or numbers in mono, uppercase, tracked 0.14em, in ink-faint.
Do put three or more siblings in one ruled ledger sharing column tracks.
Do hold body-level prose to --prose (28rem) and figures, tables and apparatus to --measure (40rem), and define both only in lesson.css.
Do print a count where a progress bar is tempting.
Do build tone from line density at 0.6px, and keep an empty state as unengraved plate.
Do self-host any new face under course/assets/fonts/ with its licence file, and keep the OpenDyslexic reading option working.
Do leave the focus ring alone: 2px focus blue at 2px offset, from print.css.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, or spend olive on anything but the 720 pass mark.
Don't raise light-theme clay line work from #ad5533 to #d97757; it measures 2.96:1 on ivory.
Don't ship a box-shadow, text-shadow, drop-shadow or gradient in any state.
Don't add a border radius, including on SVG rects and including "just for the avatar".
Don't lay out equal-size cards in a grid where a ruled index belongs.
Don't put more than one filled colour field on a sheet.
Don't let ornament - rosette, guilloche, seal, plate borders - into a question body or a timed screen.
Don't stack a lone section number above a heading; it goes inline, in mono, at 0.82em.
Don't declare an @font-face for Styrene A or Copernicus, or reference anthropicSans / anthropicSerif: they are licensed and not in this repo.

Don't redefine --prose, --measure or any palette token outside the file that owns it, and don't delete the legacy aliases (paper, accent, accent-dim, good, bad, flag, code-bg, grid, muted, text-secondary, success-text, critical) - live markup and nav.css fallback chains still name them.
